open_points.subject: import closure
open_points.text: “after the first successful production import the operation is closed and refused” conflicts with “Each source's first successful import into production closes the operation for that source” and “the VPS and the test rig may each be imported successfully once”
open_points.question: Does one successful import close all importing, or may production accept one successful import from each of the VPS and test rig?
options: Close importing after the first source succeeds
Allow one successful import per source
open_points.default_guess: Allow one successful import from each named source.

open_points.subject: unknown agent session access
open_points.text: “an unknown session answers that it has no access” conflicts with “A call naming a session that is not registered is refused like a call outside the set”
open_points.question: When Kernel reads access for an unregistered session, does Registry return an empty access result or the indistinguishable refusal required for unregistered agent-authority calls?
options: Return an empty access result
Return the same refusal as an unauthorized or nonexistent target

open_points.subject: declined access request outcome
open_points.text: “declining changes nothing; the session reads the outcome in its access” while the access output contains only “granted project ids, its active project if any, and the access version”
open_points.question: What observable fact tells the session that its pending request was declined rather than still pending or never answered?
options: Expose request status in the access result
Change the access version and define that as the outcome signal
Provide a separate request-status result
open_points.default_guess: Expose the pending request's resolved status in the access result.

open_points.subject: registered-session discovery
open_points.text: “the owner sees the registered sessions in the owner interface” but no action lists or otherwise discovers registered sessions
open_points.question: What Registry action lets the owner discover the sessions for which access can be read, granted, changed or revoked?
options: List registered sessions
Show sessions only through a combined access-request queue
Require an externally supplied session identity
open_points.default_guess: Add an owner-only list of registered sessions.

open_points.subject: pending-request discovery
open_points.text: “the owner sees in the owner interface” and “the customer, audit and switch-request views the primary actions need” but no read or list action returns pending access requests
open_points.question: What action and output let the owner discover pending requests that can be answered?
options: List all pending requests
List requests for a selected session
Include pending requests in a session-access listing
open_points.default_guess: Add an owner-only list of pending requests with their session identities and text.

open_points.subject: session access version
open_points.text: “the access version” is returned, but no text says which grants, revocations, active-project changes, request changes, registration or expiry events advance it
open_points.question: Which accepted actions advance a session's access version, and must owner mutations state the version they were made against?
options: Advance it only when the granted set or active project changes
Advance it for every session-access or request change
Treat it as an immutable registration version
open_points.default_guess: Advance it whenever the granted set or active project changes and require it on owner access mutations.

open_points.subject: anonymised project invariant and reads
open_points.text: “A project has exactly one object” and “context therefore always has an address” conflict with anonymisation where “its name, object and customer link go”; read-project still promises a project card “with its object and rooms” for any status
open_points.question: After anonymisation, which read, list, context and agent-projection operations remain available, and what do they return when the required name, object and address no longer exist?
options: Only validate and artifact reads remain available
Return reduced representations without the removed fields
Keep non-identifying replacement values and an object shell
open_points.default_guess: Allow validate and retained-artifact reads, but refuse full project, context and agent-projection reads.

open_points.subject: erased project and session grants
open_points.text: “the project leaves the session's set” is defined only for explicit revocation, while whole-project erasure deletes a project that may remain in one or more granted sets
open_points.question: Does anonymising or deleting an archived project remove it from every session's granted set and clear it when active, or may dangling grants remain?
options: Remove all grants and clear active references
Keep grants and make later operations answer archived or not found
open_points.default_guess: Remove the project from all session grants and clear active references atomically.

open_points.subject: restriction exceptions and lifting
open_points.text: “any operation using its restricted personal data is refused unless the law provides an exception” and a restriction may be lifted “where a lawful ground allows it”
open_points.question: Who decides that an exception or lawful ground applies, what input records that decision, and what Registry does when no such evidence is supplied?
options: Registry has explicit owner-confirmed exception inputs
Governance decides outside Registry and the owner merely commands the action
Registry implements no exceptions and always refuses restricted processing
open_points.default_guess: Registry refuses restricted processing except for the expressly listed owner correction and erasure actions, and treats lifting as an owner-governed command.

open_points.subject: optimistic concurrency versus idempotent repeats
open_points.text: “A change against an older revision is refused” conflicts with “archiving an archived project returns it unchanged” and “erasing an erased customer returns it unchanged” when the repeated request necessarily carries the pre-change revision
open_points.question: For an exact retry of a successful archive or customer erasure carrying the old revision, does idempotent success or stale-revision refusal take precedence?
options: Return the current unchanged record as successful replay
Refuse every stale retry
Recognize only a request-id replay as successful
open_points.default_guess: Recognize the same request as an idempotent replay; otherwise refuse the stale revision.

open_points.subject: owner confirmation
open_points.text: “owner, after confirming” and “owner, confirming” require confirmation for archive, import and archived-project erasure, but no confirmation input, observable result or missing-confirmation failure is defined
open_points.question: What constitutes confirmation for each destructive action, how is its confirmation id produced, and what happens when confirmation is absent, stale or for a different target or choice?
options: A separate confirmation token bound to action and target
A confirmation field in the same request
An owner-interface page transition with no service-level confirmation
open_points.default_guess: Use a separate short-lived confirmation token bound to the owner session, action, target, revision and selected erasure mode.

open_points.subject: agent projection content safety
open_points.text: The projection promises “no address, customer or other personal value” while it includes free-text display names, room names and artifact pointers whose `uri` or `payload_ref` content is otherwise unrestricted
open_points.question: What prevents personal data embedded in project names, room names, URIs or payload references from reaching the agent?
options: Reject personal data in all fields exposed to agents
Return redacted or separately maintained agent-safe labels and references
Remove unsafe fields from the agent projection
open_points.default_guess: Define and validate separate agent-safe display fields and opaque artifact references, omitting unverified free text and URIs.

open_points.subject: audit event coverage
open_points.text: “significant changes of state” is described as “changes to projects and customer records, granting and revoking an agent session's projects, restricting processing and lifting it, and erasures and anonymisations” without saying whether room additions, pointer publication or withdrawal, imports, session registration, active-project changes, or request creation and resolution count
open_points.question: Exactly which primary actions must append audit entries, including which agent actions justify the declared “agent through Kernel” acting principal?
options: Audit every state-changing primary action
Audit only the enumerated categories narrowly
Provide an explicit per-action audit table
open_points.default_guess: Audit every state-changing primary action and define the coverage per action.

open_points.subject: audit write failure
open_points.text: Registry promises a log entry for every covered change, but no text says what happens when the state change can be stored and its audit entry cannot
open_points.question: Must a covered state change and its audit entry commit atomically, and what observable failure occurs if the audit entry cannot be written?
options: Fail and roll back the state change
Commit the change and report degraded auditing
Queue the audit entry for later persistence
open_points.default_guess: Commit the state change and audit entry atomically; otherwise refuse the operation with nothing changed.

open_points.subject: audit-log retention
open_points.text: The audit log “is kept for a limited period the governance documents,” while “Registry erases nothing on its own” and the primary actions contain no operation for deleting expired audit entries
open_points.question: What Registry action applies the governance retention period to audit entries, and who invokes it?
options: Owner explicitly purges audit entries through a Registry action
Registry automatically expires audit entries
An external administrator deletes them outside Registry
open_points.default_guess: Provide an owner-confirmed action that purges audit entries selected by the governance review.

open_points.subject: audit target identifiers
open_points.text: Audit entries name “the project or customer” while the log holds “no personal value,” yet “a project's id is not anonymous by itself” and customer references link projects to people
open_points.question: How can an audit entry identify its project or customer without retaining a value considered personal or re-identifying after erasure?
options: Permit opaque project and customer ids in the audit log as a stated exception
Use non-linkable audit-specific identifiers
Remove target identifiers during erasure or anonymisation
open_points.default_guess: Use audit-specific non-linkable identifiers and sever their mapping when the subject is erased.

open_points.subject: Cabinet Web mirror status
open_points.text: The actor list says the Cabinet Web mirror is a consumer and “Each authenticates with its own service token,” while R0-27 says it “keeps its read only if it receives a token of its own”
open_points.question: Is the Cabinet Web mirror an admitted current consumer with a configured token, or merely a retired candidate with no access unless separately enabled?
options: Current consumer with its own token
Disabled consumer until explicitly issued a token
Removed from the actor list
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as disabled until the owner explicitly issues its own token.

open_points.subject: onboard_object authority
open_points.text: The script is still called “a client of the API like any consumer,” but “its staff-credential use ends with R0-30” and “its role is taken by the owner interface and Kernel flows”; no remaining token or permitted action is named
open_points.question: Is `onboard_object` retired and unable to call production Registry, or does it retain some authenticated role and operation set?
options: Retire it completely
Give it a dedicated service identity and limited operations
Allow only owner-mediated use through the owner interface
